newsitem.title: JAPAN: Natural to hike rates if economy strong - Sakakibara.
newsitem.headline: Natural to hike rates if economy strong - Sakakibara.

text.p: Senior Ministry of Finance (MOF) official Eisuke Sakakibara told Reuters on Friday that it would be natural for the Bank of Japan (BOJ) to raise interest rates when it has confirmed the strength of the economy.

Sakakibara, director-general of the ministry's International Finance Bureau, also told Reuters in an interview that it would be dangerous for financial markets to assume that Japan will not raise rates within the next year.
"Current interest rate levels are abnormal and it would be natural if those levels were to be normalised in the future," he said.

Asked what demerits a rise in Japan's interest rates would produce, Sakakibara said operating profits of Japanese banks would not drop even if short-term interest rates were to be raised by 0.25 or 0.5 percentage point.

"It's entirely up to the BOJ to consider a change in its monetary policy. But raising interest rates would be a natural action for the BOJ to take when it has confirmed the strength of the economy," he said.

He said there are many people who are dissatisfied with current interest rate levels. "The political mood (about interest rates) can be a factor (in considering a change in Japan's monetary policy)," he said.
"It would be dangerous to assume that Japan will definitely not raise interest rates for the next 12 months," he said.
The interview with Sakakibara was broadcast by Reuters Financial Television.
